title: Complete Riverhog source corpus, valid GuavaJam supporting-source adapter, and modeled text reuse
scope: Research evidence for generic GuavaJam source acceptance and static search; no Riverhog software-version semantics are added to GuavaJam.
The complete current native Contract Closure inventory is used, not the earlier 4,258-symbol proxy.
This guide and the retained scripts are reference evidence. They are not a production Riverhog migration or GuavaJam implementation.

riverhog.generation: The unmodified source-owned contract_candidate.py generate command produced the complete Closure, separate Audit Record, and validated native atlas from a clean exact checkout. It exited 0.
riverhog.boundary: Generated reports describe source-owned contracts; they do not create new promises. Riverhog owns release-to-documentation-edition mapping, applicability membership, contract equivalence and compatibility.
riverhog.documentation_obligations: Existing Riverhog policy binds release prose to native CLI, OpenAPI, Python, distribution, OCI and reference outputs; requires ancestry-independent documentation history; and preserves already-published version subtrees. A site migration must explicitly preserve or redesign those Riverhog-owned obligations.
riverhog.authored_release_input: The inspected release-documentation commit 9fb4a7d52b12a61e582be5656471979e8ee5e1e4 contained only its three root setup files. No populated authored release manual was available or claimed as this corpus.

complete_native_corpus.extraction: Each real Closure element contributes native human-contract text from its own generated element page. Audit/navigation controls and the duplicate exact-machine-fields panel are excluded from searchable text; no native chunk text is truncated.
complete_native_corpus.omission_reason: Large reproducible outputs are not duplicated in the reference commit; the complete valid production-NAV fixture is retained compressed for fast search reproduction.

complete_valid_supporting_source.method: Each native heading chunk becomes an escaped literal paragraph with its own explicit anchor. A separately anchored metadata introduction is produced by GuavaJam. The production loader accepts every file, and every original chunk roundtrips through production NAV with identical text.
complete_valid_supporting_source.layout_limit: The flat paragraphs are a lossless visible-text benchmark adapter, not the final table/list/link presentation. A large native table can remain a roughly one-megabyte paragraph; production editorial layout and link preservation need their own adapter qualification.
complete_valid_supporting_source.navigation_layout_warning: GuavaJam emits both heading-section text and individual anchored body-block text. H2 plus body can nearly double passage rows/bytes while leaving document text unchanged. Do not use the flat fixture count as a guarantee for another renderer layout.
complete_valid_supporting_source.record_shape: id, title, abstract, path, metadata, navigation{text,anchors}, source_markdown_sha256, source_markdown_bytes, native_source_html_sha256
complete_valid_supporting_source.consumer_warning: navigation.text already includes the document title. navigation.anchors already includes the metadata passage. All anchor titles/kinds/levels/positions/parents/scopes are production-derived. Actual metadata text separates labels and values with whitespace, not synthetic colon/semicolon punctuation.

source_fidelity.initial_source_bytes: All 5,947 v2 initial document hashes and byte counts agree with the real supporting GFM accepted by the production parser; all 36,063 anchor records and all literal metadata memberships agree with the retained NAV input.
source_fidelity.modeled_source_bytes: The v2 storage experiment serializes exact flat GFM for modeled subsequent editions and hashes those real serialized bytes. It does not retain a stale original text alias in transformed passage records.
source_fidelity.provenance_limit: Modeled edition revisions, dates, work-level facts and citation routes remain explicit benchmark context. Real source-byte hashes do not turn those modeled revisions into signed Git publications.
not_claimed: Full final renderer and citation/browser qualification

policy.selection: random_5_percent samples round(N*0.05) document identities independently each update; largest_5_percent repeatedly changes the same initial largest round(N*0.05) bodies; all changes every document.
policy.passage_change: Both last-passage (matching storage_matrix.py) and largest-passage sensitivity are reported. The selected original passage gets a unique edition-number marker appended; later changes replace the prior marker rather than accumulate history.
policy.metadata: none: content only (including document title for NAV input). stable: literal Authority, Interface, Element ID and Label. edition: additionally Example version vN, changing every edition. Visible metadata is one extra passage. NAV input uses exact production metadata_block/source_text and exact title/metadata/content order; heading input retains the earlier colon/semicolon presentation model.
policy.identity: Exact UTF-8 body strings deduplicated by SHA-256; payload bytes exclude hashes, keys, references, SQLite pages, FTS postings/docsize, ranking fields, citation data, frontmatter syntax, compression and source-GFM segmentation overhead.
policy.source_changes: Count is a consequence of modeled body/metadata changes with other source fields fixed; it is not an exact serialized source-file size or hash measurement.
policy.limits: Synthetic editions of actual production supporting-GFM/navigation text, not real Riverhog release history, database-size estimates, or browser qualification. Flat literal paragraphs are a text-preserving benchmark adapter, not final table/link presentation.

interpretation: Document-count churn does not describe changed-byte volume: the largest 297 native documents contain about 8.64 million bytes.

Changing visible version metadata makes every whole document-body string different even when native content is unchanged. Store native blocks and metadata introductions separately if exact reconstructed document text is to retain that reuse.

These measurements count SHA-256-distinct UTF-8 strings only. They are not SQLite, FTS-posting, compressed-transfer, RAM or latency estimates. Retaining occurrence-level FTS ranking is a separate requirement.

Stable metadata in the sensitivity model omits Example version; per-edition mode adds vN. The storage experiment may retain v1 when its stable mode is selected. Read each experiment's explicit metadata definition before comparing numbers.

environment_variables.PROFFER_REFERENCE: Absolute path to this retained .reference directory.
environment_variables.GUAVAJAM_RESEARCH_OUTPUT: Fresh absolute output directory outside both source checkouts.
environment_variables.GUAVAJAM_CHECKOUT: Separate checkout at 54fce07b619628a5e92be946be4b189873ddf1a0, not the later reference commit.
environment_variables.RIVERHOG_ENV: External uv environment using Python 3.12.3 and Riverhog locked workspace dependencies.
environment_variables.GUAVAJAM_ENV: External uv environment using Python 3.12.12 and GuavaJam locked runtime dependencies.
environment_variables.PANDOC_BINARY: Actual Pandoc 3.12.1 binary, not a version-check bypass.

pitfalls: The reference commit adds evidence files and therefore is not the baseline SHA accepted by the adapter. Use separate pinned clean source checkouts; do not weaken its identity checks.

Riverhog generation requires its full locked workspace environment, not a few copied Python modules. Observed generation was 763.33 seconds with approximately 900 MiB peak child RSS; do not label that cost GuavaJam performance.
The retained fast-path NAV fixture avoids regenerating the large native atlas for every search experiment.
Python and uv versions differ between Riverhog and GuavaJam as specified above. Pandoc must actually be 3.12.1. The retained environment receipt describes the observed Linux runtime.

Whole-repository GuavaJam validation retains its stock 128-document aggregate guard. This adapter directly qualifies all supporting blobs and NAV extraction; aggregate guard removal and complete source/render publication remain separately scoped evidence.
The native corpus manifest references larger omitted intermediate files. Regenerate them through the full source path; they are intentionally not present in this reference package.
Environment receipts and elapsed timings can vary by host. Inputs, source/code hashes and exact content outcomes are the reproducibility anchors.
Do not treat synthetic edition dates or revision digests as actual Riverhog release history, and do not infer release applicability from changed-in metadata alone.
